BiblicalUsage: All thy garments smell of myrrh, and aloes, and cassia, out of the ivory palaces, says the psalmist. The word is the spice itself, cassia bark, perfuming the royal robe.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the king's garments smelling of cassia is a picture of gladness, and the psalmist says the ivory palaces made him glad.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
